title: A leader accepts a write it cannot commit
summary: An isolated Raft leader can append a proposal locally, but proposal acceptance is not commit evidence and the state machine must remain unchanged without a majority.
trigger: Elect node 1, isolate it from nodes 2 and 3, then propose an unsafe write on the old leader.
observed: The proposal is appended locally while the commit index remains fixed and the MVCC store never exposes the value.
invariant: No command may become committed or visible until an entry from the leader's current term is replicated to a majority.
fix: Treat proposal acceptance as local admission only; advance commit and apply state strictly after majority acknowledgement.

timeline.title: Cut the leader away
timeline.detail: Node 1 retains its old leadership state while every transport edge to the majority is removed.

timeline.title: Append without quorum
timeline.detail: The write enters node 1's private log; no majority acknowledgement exists.

timeline.title: Commit index does not move
timeline.detail: The test records the pre-partition index and proves it is unchanged after delivery.

timeline.title: State machine stays clean
timeline.detail: A timestamped read returns no unsafe value; the majority elects a different leader and commits safely.

timeline.title: Bind the evidence
timeline.detail: Receipt binds the exact commit, test lines, command identifier, and expected assertion total.

limits: The deterministic transport models exact partitions, not TCP timeouts, kernel scheduling, or fsync latency.
